title: Is godot okay for 3d games or should I switch to unity?
author: TheUniverseOrNothing
selftext:
I’ve been making a 3d climbing game with realistic mountains and 3d graphics. Godot has been great but it does lack 3d character movement. It’s not terrible but it still looks a little off. 

The overall gameplay and function work fine. And I’m enjoying playing the game. I know that solid gameplay will outperform the graphics. But while I’m having fable 5.2 and opus 5.5 doing great work with blender I’m heavily debating if I should just make the switch now?

When I discuss this with Claude it suggests that godot has more than enough 3d ability and could still get my character to that level with just a little more effort.

Any advice on this?

comments.author: Any-Blacksmith-2054
comments.body: Godot is ok with animations, if you don't like ones created by Claude you can always download free ones from Mixamo and Claude will apply them

comments.author: TheUniverseOrNothing
comments.body:
I already feel like my game in godot is starting to look good, not great, but not terrible.

I would not say it’s beautiful or triple AAA level by any means.

I’m just wondering if there hasn’t been enough time and people are reciting old information as far what godot can produce in 3d now.

comments.author: Pleyar
comments.body: Godot can do very good 3d just not photorealistic

replies.author: TheUniverseOrNothing
replies.body:
Good to know. Claude is building a section of my mountain in unreal engine and going to compare side by side how it looked.

Getting it photorealistic wouldn’t change gameplay but scene and environment are huge in my game.

comments.author: Necessary_Weight
comments.body: Godot is extremely well suited to AI dev. It is good enough for 3d - check out Road to Vostok which is 3d in godot

comments.author: Arkenhammer
comments.body: The main difference between 3D graphics engines is the lighting. If you are having trouble with animation, switching engine isn’t likely to help you.

comments.author: Spudly42
comments.body: For AI development, I have to assume whatever tool is fastest for compiling and replaying quicky will be the best. I've used Unity quite a while and they're making improvements there, but you still spend a good bit of time with various compiling, domain reloading, initializing, etc.  No idea how godot is on that front, though.

replies.author: TheUniverseOrNothing
replies.body:
From my experience Godot has been great which is why I’m questioning everyone saying it’s horrible 3d.

I think it’s outdated information + AI has taken leaps in the past year.
